source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: A student asked whether you have to explicitly tell an agent to use a particular skill, or whether it happens automatically. What was the answer?

options.text: A skill only ever loads when it is explicitly named by its exact file path
options.feedback: Requiring an exact path would defeat the point of automatic matching. Loading turns on how closely a request matches the skill's name and description, not on typing a location.

options.text: Skills always require a human to approve loading them before every single use
options.feedback: No per-use approval step was described. Automatic matching is exactly what lets a skill trigger without that kind of gatekeeping on every request.

options.text: It should load automatically when a request matches its name and description
options.feedback: That match is the whole reason those two fields stay resident in context. You can also call a skill explicitly, often with a forward-slash command, but recognition is the normal path.

options.text: Automatic loading is impossible; every skill must be invoked with a slash command
options.feedback: Explicit invocation is available as an option, not as the only route. Automatic loading on a close match was described as how a skill is normally reached.
